summary: Tajikistan waives visas for about 80 nationalities — including the EU, US, Canada, Australia and Japan — for stays of up to 30 days, and most CIS citizens enter with no time limit. About 130 nationalities, including the UK, can apply online for an eVisa (with an optional GBAO permit for the Pamir Highway); the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Tajikistan. Border officials apply this rule to both visa-free and eVisa travelers.

currencyLimits.text: Cash above USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival, with documents showing where the money came from. Up to USD 3,000 can be taken out without a declaration. Keep your entry declaration until you leave.

notes: Drones may not be brought in without prior permission. They are routinely confiscated at the border.
Carry a doctor's letter for strong prescription painkillers; some codeine- and tramadol-based medicines are controlled substances.

payments.text: Tajikistan runs on cash. Cards work in a handful of Dushanbe hotels and supermarkets, and ATMs are unreliable outside Dushanbe and Khujand. Bring crisp US dollar notes to change as you go.

safety.text: Travelers are generally welcomed, but pickpocketing is common in crowded places in Dushanbe, and terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks. The considerations are practical: rough roads, high altitude on the Pamir Highway, and border areas with Afghanistan and Kyrgyzstan that can be restricted or close at short notice.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tajikistan travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring and early fall are ideal in the lowland cities; the high Pamir Highway is best from late June to September, when the passes are reliably open.

idp.text: Tajikistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Tajikistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Tajikistan yet.

tips.text: The Pamir Highway runs through the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO), which needs its own permit on top of your visa or visa waiver — eVisa applicants can simply tick the GBAO box on evisa.tj; visa-free travelers should arrange it through OVIR in Dushanbe or a local tour operator.
Check border and GBAO access status shortly before traveling — sections of the Afghan and Kyrgyz border areas, and occasionally GBAO itself, are closed to foreigners at short notice.
Bring enough cash for your whole trip in clean, newer US dollar bills — exchange offices reject worn notes, and ATMs beyond Dushanbe and Khujand often have no money or no card connection.

Visa-free visitors must register with the authorities within 10 working days of arrival, and hotels can no longer do it for you — go to the registration office (OVIR) in Dushanbe. eVisa holders are exempt from registration.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tajikistan?
faq.answer: About 80 nationalities — including all EU countries, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea — can visit visa-free for up to 30 days, and most CIS citizens enter visa-free with no time limit. British and Israeli citizens need a visa and can apply for the eVisa at evisa.tj, as can about 130 nationalities in all; the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Tajikistan?
faq.answer: No — US passport holders can enter Tajikistan visa-free for up to 30 days. For a longer trip, apply for the 60-day eVisa at evisa.tj before travel.

faq.question: What is the GBAO permit and do I need it for the Pamir Highway?
faq.answer: The Pamir Highway crosses the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region, which requires a separate GBAO permit for all foreigners. eVisa applicants add it for USD 20 during the online application; visa-free travelers arrange it in Dushanbe through OVIR or a tour agency. Carry several copies. It is checked at police posts along the route.

faq.question: How much does the Tajikistan eVisa cost and how long does it take?
faq.answer: The single-entry tourist eVisa costs USD 50, allows a stay of up to 60 days and is normally issued within one to three working days at evisa.tj. Adding the GBAO permit costs USD 20 more.

faq.question: Can I enter Tajikistan overland with an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes. The eVisa and the visa waiver are accepted at the main road borders with Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan as well as at Dushanbe airport. Print your eVisa and GBAO permit, and confirm the specific crossing is open before setting out, as smaller posts close periodically.
